kind.description: Deprecated, derived composite: the value is stack + '-' + role, or the bare role when stack is 'none'. Never authored by hand and never newly required. It stays in `required` only so an undocumented consumer of the composite keeps parsing. A stack-qualified value present alongside two declared axes, or a kind that disagrees with the value derived from its own axes, is WARNING TAXONOMY_LEGACY_VALUE. A kind that is neither in the legacy 'kinds' vocabulary nor the value derived from its own two declared axes is KIND_UNKNOWN. Kind never drives profile requirements.

role.description: What the project is for. Independent of `stack`; every role/stack combination is legal. Must use a canonical value from vocabulary.json roles; absent or non-canonical is WARNING TAXONOMY_AXIS_UNKNOWN. Descriptive: never drives required files, CI, verification, or any evidence state.

stack.description: What the project is written in. Single-valued by owner ruling; there is no `stacks` array. Must use a canonical value from vocabulary.json stacks; absent or non-canonical is WARNING TAXONOMY_AXIS_UNKNOWN. Descriptive: never drives required files, CI, verification, or any evidence state.

profile.description: Governance profile driving required files, CI, OpenSpec and verification requirements. Must use a canonical value from vocabulary.json profiles.

database_source.description: How the runtime reaches PostgreSQL. 'container' (default for *-postgres templates) starts a per-project container; 'external' (for *-postgres-external templates) reads a connection from a gitignored .env or host secret source and starts no database container.

capabilities.description: Optional capability declarations. Each key is a capability name (e.g. identity, admin, tenancy, billing, jobs, storage, release). Declarations are intent, not implementation evidence.

declines.description: Optional evidence-backed non-adoption records. A decline is the lawful exit from a capability adoption finding other than adopting the provider. See docs/capabilities.md.

adoption_grant.description: A bounded, single-use, expiring permission for one named actor to repoint THIS repository onto one registered shared provider for one capability, without separate cross-repo authorization. The provider repository is read-only at all times. The executed outcome is appended to adoption/adoptions.json. See docs/adoption-grant.md.

capability.description: A capability id that must ALREADY be bound to this provider in capabilities.json. A grant may not create the binding it consumes.

provider.description: Registered project id of the shared provider. The provider root is never writable under this grant.

package.description: The published package the consumer is permitted to pin, e.g. 'Platform.Idempotency'.

version.description: The exact provider version this grant authorizes. Consuming a different version is a provider change and is refused as ADOPTION_GRANT_SCOPE_VIOLATION.

actor.description: The single agent session the grant binds, e.g. 'agent:<session-id>'.

issued_at.description: Issue timestamp (ISO 8601). A grant is not active before this time.

expires_at.description: Mandatory expiry (ISO 8601) so a grant cannot silently become standing authorization. A past expiry is ADOPTION_GRANT_STALE and does not retroactively legalize a repoint.

write_set.description: Repository-relative glob patterns the grant may write. Every pattern must resolve inside this repository's root. Patterns naming the provider, the promotion ledger, or a source-level coupling are refused.

rollback_ref.description: How to undo the repoint, e.g. an OpenSpec change id. Recorded verbatim in the adoption row.

status.description: Defaults to 'active'. A revoked grant is ADOPTION_GRANT_STALE for any further repoint.

release_evidence.description: Optional release evidence record. Each field is one of revision, version, toolchain, artifacts, digests, sbom, provenance, checks, publication. Missing or unverified fields do not satisfy a deployable gate.

quality.description: Optional product-code quality policy consumed by scripts/product_code_quality.py. Declares product source roots, supported languages, exclusions, and the placeholder marker threshold.

product_roots.description: Repository-relative directories that count as product source. Each must exist and be a directory.

exclude.description: Repository-relative paths under any product root to exclude (generated, vendor, fixture, etc.). Exclusions must not escape the project root.

placeholder_threshold.description: Maximum number of placeholder markers (TODO, FIXME, etc.) tolerated across all product files before the check fails.

placeholder_markers.description: Override the default placeholder marker vocabulary. Words are matched case-insensitively with word boundaries.

standalone.description: Optional declaration of how a project operates without sibling checkouts or private external services. Declarations are intent, not implementation evidence; the audit uses the shape to derive a classification but never executes project commands.

status.description: One of the six canonical statuses from vocabulary.json.standalone_statuses.

local_defaults.description: Repository-relative entries the project uses to satisfy its baseline (e.g. 'sqlite', 'local-fixtures'). Each must be a non-empty, portable, repository-relative path or identifier; absolute paths and '..' segments are rejected.

required_external_services.description: Service identifiers required for the baseline (e.g. 'postgres', 's3'). Each must be a portable, repository-relative identifier; absolute paths and '..' segments are rejected.

required_sibling_projects.description: Sibling project ids required for the baseline. Each must match a canonical project id (kebab-case). The audit does not verify the sibling exists; it only records the donation-readiness signal.

evidence_ref.description: Repository-relative path to the native evidence artefact (e.g. docs/standalone.md). Absolute paths and '..' segments are rejected. Required when evidence_state is 'configured' or 'verified'.

evidence_state.description: Lifecycle state of the standalone block. The audit enforces the same shape rules as for release_evidence.

integrations.description: Optional list of named external providers the project optionally or mandatorily integrates with. Each entry is a JSON object; absolute paths in 'evidence_ref' are rejected.

interfaces.description: Optional declaration of the boundaries this project provides and consumes. Each entry names one reachable interface: a stable kebab-case 'id', exactly one of 'provides'/'consumes', a 'mechanism' from the closed set invoke|consume|observe|sibling, and an 'entry' in that mechanism's vocabulary. An absent array means 'nothing declared' and produces no finding, so a project that declares nothing is never charged for a boundary it did not claim. Interface ids must be unique within the project; uniqueness is enforced by the audit because JSON Schema cannot express it. See docs/capabilities.md.

taxonomy_role.description: Canonical role axis. The vocabulary.json.roles list is the source of truth; this enum mirrors it so editors that consult the schema see the same values. `shared-library` is NOT a role: by owner ruling the repositories that wrote it take role 'platform'.

taxonomy_stack.description: Canonical stack axis. The vocabulary.json.stacks list is the source of truth; this enum mirrors it so editors that consult the schema see the same values. Single-valued by owner ruling; `none` means contracts/documents/schemas with no implementation language.

standalone_status.description: Canonical standalone classification. The vocabulary.json.standalone_statuses list is the source of truth; this enum mirrors it so editors that consult the schema see the same values.

required.description: true ⇒ the provider is part of the project's baseline; false ⇒ the provider is optional and the baseline still works without it.

evidence_ref.description: Repository-relative path to the native evidence artefact. Required when 'required' is true; the audit emits STANDALONE_INTEGRATION_PENDING if the file is missing.

interface.description: One declared boundary of a project. The entry says which side of the edge this project is on, how the other side is reached, and what the contract is; the audit charges an undeclared or unpinned edge.

id.description: Stable kebab-case interface id, unique within the project.

provides.description: true when this project provides the interface.

consumes.description: true when this project consumes the interface. `provider` is then required, and the provider must declare a matching `provides` entry.

provider.description: Kebab-case id of the project (or sibling checkout) that provides the consumed interface. A consumes entry whose provider declares no matching `provides` entry is a one-sided edge reported as INTERFACE_PROVIDER_UNDECLARED.

entry.description: The interface's entry point in its mechanism's vocabulary: an argv invocation (invoke, sibling), a published package coordinate (consume), or a repository-relative document path (observe). An absolute path is never lawful.

required.description: Consumer side: true when the consumed interface is part of the project's baseline. For `mechanism: sibling` it is also the pinning flag — a sibling edge without it is INTERFACE_SIBLING_PATH_UNPINNED.

evidence_ref.description: Repository-relative path to the consumer's own evidence that it uses this interface. A consumption edge whose evidence_ref is absent or does not resolve is INTERFACE_CONSUMED_UNUSED.

allOf.description: A consumption names the provider it consumes from.
Every mechanism except `sibling` names a versioned contract: "<name>/<major>.<minor>.<patch>".
An `observe` entry is a document at a path inside the repository: no `..` segment may escape it.

interface_mechanism.description: The closed mechanism set. `invoke`: bounded argv plus one versioned JSON document. `consume`: a published artifact pinned by version and digest. `observe`: a read-only document at a declared path, digest-pinned. `sibling`: a repository-relative invocation of another checkout, lawful only when the consuming project declares that provider `required: true` and pins the edge with a digest.

interface_contract.description: A contract identifier with its version: "<name>/<major>.<minor>.<patch>", where the name is kebab-case, dotted or scoped. Required for every mechanism except `sibling`. A contract that names no version is reported as INTERFACE_CONTRACT_UNVERSIONED.

interface_digest.description: A sha256 digest of the pinned bytes or invocation. Required for `consume`, `observe` and `sibling`; a retained copy whose declared digest is not the retained bytes is INTERFACE_VENDORED_WITHOUT_DIGEST.

language.description: A language profile supported by the product-code quality checker.

evidence_state.description: Lifecycle state of a capability or evidence field. declared: project intends to provide it. configured: artefacts exist locally. verified: native evidence recorded with a ref. unverified: missing or invalid evidence. blocked: explicit non-goal.

release_evidence_state.description: Lifecycle state of a release-evidence field. The 'blocked' state is reserved for capability declarations.

owner.description: Who owns the implementation: a platform repo id, a product name, or 'shared'.

evidence_ref.description: Repository-relative path to the native evidence artefact when evidence_state is 'configured' or 'verified'.

consumes.description: Additive consumer-side consumption edges. The audit joins this record with capabilities.json and the project's own manifests; all three must agree before the capability counts as adopted. A declaration is intent, not a verification of behaviour.

provider.description: Registered project id providing the package. Must match the provider the capability binds to in capabilities.json.

package.description: Published package name the consumer pins, e.g. 'Platform.Idempotency'.

version.description: The exact pinned version. A floating range is not a consumption edge.

evidence_ref.description: Repository-relative path to the consumer's own evidence for the edge. An absolute or '..'-bearing value is refused and never normalized; a value that stops resolving emits CAPABILITY_ADOPTION_EVIDENCE_STALE.

local_implementation.description: Repository-relative path, or list of paths, of a local implementation this adoption would replace. Bounded to declaration-supplied paths: the audit never infers an undeclared duplicate.

decline.description: An evidence-backed decision not to adopt a capability. A decline exempts this project for this capability only; it never suppresses a finding in another project or for another capability.

capability.description: A capability id registered in capabilities.json.

rationale.description: Closed boundary vocabulary. Any other value emits CAPABILITY_ADOPTION_DECLINE_UNRECORDED and does not exempt the capability.

evidence_ref.description: Repository-relative document stating the boundary. Required: an assertion is not a boundary argument, and a decline without a resolving document is reported.

review_by.description: Advisory review date. It never auto-expires a decline; a stale decline is a governance conversation, not a machine decision.

value.description: Field value: a string for revision/version/toolchain/provenance, an array of strings for checks, a list of digest references for digests/sbom, or omitted when only state is known.

evidence_ref.description: Repository-relative path to the native evidence artefact when state is 'configured' or 'verified'.
